text:
First decide the parent structure and the numbering.

1. Principal characteristic group  
   –COOH is the highest-ranking group, so the parent is benzoic acid and its carbon is C-1.

2. Place the remaining substituents around the ring as stated  
   • Two ortho to the acid: –OH and –NMe₂ → they must be at C-2 and C-6.  
   • Para to the acid: –OCH₃ → C-4.  
   • –CN is meta both to –COOH and to the other two senior groups (–CHO and –COOH) and must be ortho to both –OH (C-2) and –OCH₃ (C-4); therefore –CN is at C-3.  
   • The remaining meta position to –COOH is C-5, which therefore bears the –CHO (formyl) group.

   This gives the substitution pattern:

   1 COOH (benzoic acid parent)  
   2 OH  
   3 CN  
   4 OCH₃  
   5 CHO (formyl)  
   6 NMe₂

3. Check numbering direction  
   If the ring were numbered in the opposite direction the locants would be  
   2-(dimethylamino), 3-formyl, 4-methoxy, 5-cyano, 6-hydroxy.  
   Both orientations give the same set {2,3,4,5,6}; the tie is broken by the rule that the preferred
   numbering is the one that gives the lowest locant to the substituent cited first in the name
   (which must be ordered alphabetically).  
   Alphabetically the first prefix is “cyano”, and 3 (first orientation) is lower than 5 (second
   orientation). Hence the first orientation is correct.

4. Assemble the name  
   List the prefixes alphabetically (ignoring multiplicative prefixes such as di-):

   3-cyano  
   6-(dimethylamino)  
   5-formyl  
   2-hydroxy  
   4-methoxy  

   Followed by the parent “benzoic acid”.

   Resulting name:  
   3-cyano-6-(dimethylamino)-5-formyl-2-hydroxy-4-methoxybenzoic acid

Among the given choices this corresponds to option (C).

Answer: C
